TOP SECRET
AGENT FILE #7741
Mission briefing · read before you move

Six weeks ago you crossed the border under a name that wasn't yours, carrying a microfilm that wasn't supposed to exist. The target: proof that the regime's Ministry of Language Purity wasn't just enforcing grammar — it was weaponising it. Every misplaced modal verb, every dangling tense, became a pretext. A pretext to detain. To disappear. To silence.

You almost made it out clean. Almost.

One slip at the border checkpoint — a present perfect where a simple past belonged — was all the guard needed. In this country, that isn't a mistake. That's a confession.

Now you're Prisoner 7741, locked inside a maximum-security facility where every wall has ears and every syllable is evidence on file. Your handlers have gone dark. No extraction team is coming. If you're getting out, you're getting out on your own grammar.

THE ESCAPE PLAN

Intelligence gathered before capture — and scraps picked up since — point to exactly one route out. Not the easiest one. The only one.

01
🏃 The Rooftops

You move at night, above the wire, above the searchlights. Ground-floor corridors are watched too closely for a direct approach — but the roofs are patrolled thinly, littered with old signage and half-broken propaganda placards from decommissioned watch posts. Why start here: it's the only stretch of the facility where speed matters more than stealth, and where a wrong turn only costs you time, not your cover.

02
🥊 The Checkpoint

Every route down from the roofs funnels through one guarded post — no way around it, only through. Talk your way past if you can. If talk fails and the Warden steps in himself, you settle it the only way this prison understands: a duel of sentences, fought like a physical fight. Why here, why now: it's a chokepoint by design — clear it once, cleanly, and the alarm never has a reason to sound.

03
💬 The Holding Room

Past the checkpoint, you're funnelled into the common block before anyone questions why you're still moving. This is where the real prisoners are — the ones who've survived by reading tone, not just words. Why here: you need eyes and ears you don't have. An ally won the right way here is worth more than any key you could steal.

04
🧑‍🏫 The Library

Deeper in, past checkpoints you were never meant to reach, sits the archive — transcripts, banned grammar texts, the Ministry's own case files. The librarian guards it like a second warden. She can't be bribed. She might, however, be convinced — if you ask her exactly the right way. Why here: the record of every "error" ever filed against you is the one thing that can clear your name outside these walls.

05
🔐 The Locked Doors

Everything gathered — every ally, every hint, every fragment of proof — buys you one shot at the final block: the vault room, the logic room, the terminal that controls the outer gate. Why last: these doors don't open for force, and they don't open for luck. Only for someone who's proven, step by step, that they can't be caught out by this language anymore.

Six weeks in. One shot out. Move fast, speak precisely — and don't let a single dangling modifier get you killed.
